entries.name: Orthodox Christmas (Božić)
entries.capsule: Christmas for Serbian Orthodox Christians, including Bosnian Serbs, on January 7, with Christmas Eve on January 6.
entries.dateRule: December 25 on the Julian calendar, which is January 7 on the Gregorian calendar from 1900 to 2099. Each entry below is the January 7 that falls in that calendar year.

entries.name: Srebrenica Genocide Remembrance Day
alsoKnownAs: International Day of Reflection and Commemoration of the 1995 Genocide in Srebrenica
entries.capsule: Remembers more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys killed at Srebrenica in July 1995; marked in Rochester with a peace march.
entries.dateRule: July 11 each year. Designated by the U.N. General Assembly on May 23, 2024.

dates.source: U.N. General Assembly resolution 78/282 designates July 11 annually
Fixed date, U.N. resolution
Fixed date, U.N. resolution

entries.whatItMarks: The July 1995 genocide at Srebrenica, when Bosnian Serb forces overran a U.N. safe area and killed at least 8,000 Bosniak men and boys.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In Rochester in 2025, Bosnian residents held the city's first peace march around Cascade Lake on Friday, July 11, followed by an all-day soccer tournament at the Watson Sports Complex on Saturday. An organizer said many Bosnians in Rochester are survivors or lost loved ones. No Twin Cities observance and no Minnesota proclamation were found; no 2026 Rochester announcement was found.

entries.whatItMarks: Thanks to the United States around the Fourth of July and remembrance of Srebrenica.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Started about 2011 by three Bosnian-born Rochester men. In 2013 six teams played at Watson Soccer Complex, including the Rochester team United BiH and a Bosnian team from Des Moines; a Rochester Somali team won. The director addressed players about July 1995 before the games. In 2025 the tournament was held July 12 as part of the 30th anniversary remembrance.
